findings: Declare the ambient data before introducing cofactor degeneracy; keep the general setting distinct from later dimensional and geometric specializations.
Track regularity and connectedness hypotheses in each uniqueness mechanism, and the exact support/zero-set properties of the counterexamples.
The extrema theorem retains C1,1 potentials, continuous common density, a positive test metric, and separate component criteria for uniform cofactor ellipticity and the positive-density region.

Good-contact and measurable strong-maximum proofs use almost-everywhere Hessians and no derivatives of the matrix coefficients. The hypersurface argument uses unordered local sides rather than orientability.
The square-root threshold uses C1,1 nonnegative density and transverse segments; keep the later sharpness examples as its actual dependency.
Weighted cofactor energy requires only continuous positive weight and distributional dd^c-closedness; unweighted orbit propagation has separate range-field regularity and orbit-density hypotheses.

The low-dimensional Sobolev argument uses strong W2,n approximation and signed algebra, whereas bounded connected-density uniqueness uses level energy and concentrated smooth tests. These do not impose a metric mass property.
Ordinary comparison under Guan–Li gives bounded Lp uniqueness without a connected positive-density set. Its condition belongs to the equation background.
The projective examples progress from an open zero band to two flat hypersurfaces, quadratic zeros, and a globally real analytic density. Preserve the exact ranks and the smooth extension arguments.

The analytic-density introduction uses t before its declaration. The Hopf specialization needs a precise recall of its projection and pulled-back form. Preserve inherited projective block notation in later constructions rather than redeclaring it.

The radial continuum proof uses matching slopes, C1,1 distributional Hessians and bounded-product compatibility; quadratic zeros force exponential flattening of the slope. The analytic example patches horizontal coefficients while preserving the prescribed determinant.

proof_checks: The C1,1 extrema argument keeps almost-everywhere Hessians, continuous density and the local essential cofactor lower bound. Tilted contacts avoid the null set; the annular barrier does not differentiate measurable coefficients. Dimension one and the unordered local sides of a connected hypersurface remain separate cases.

Quadratic growth of a nonnegative C1,1 density and transverse segments give the square-root sublevel lower bound. The liminf hypothesis eliminates local separation; the inverse-half-power criterion uses dominated convergence. The later analytic examples supply sharpness only in dimensions at least three.

The continuous weighted cofactor identity uses distributional dd^c-closedness and testing by w squared. Absolutely continuous reachable curves and locally Lipschitz control flows remain distinct. The unweighted exterior-ball argument propagates only extrema; dense-orbit and smooth bracket-generating hypotheses are not interchanged.
The unweighted energy defect has the stated sign. Gauduchon cancellation in dimension two does not extend automatically to three; the threefold formula retains its mixed torsion term.

The W2,n proof uses strong approximation, signed wedge identities and the pointwise determinant algebra in dimensions two and three. Its threefold sign condition controls the integrated quadratic form. The Hopf specialization satisfies that condition despite infinite upper mass.

The bounded proof retains continuous omega-psh potentials. Common local regularizations define a finite positive energy measure; its pushforward has a Lipschitz level density and no level atoms. Coercivity uses the ac determinant lower bound, reciprocal level cutoffs and connectedness of the positive-density set.

The smooth auxiliary tests use a sufficiently large quadratic strict subsolution, the real ABP contact estimate with the standard complex structure, and a fixed L2 density bound. Concentrated tests and weak extreme-level localization yield the bounded uniqueness statement under its actual hypotheses.

Invariant mass yields ordinary bounded comparison by locality and Chapter1 bounded ordered contact. The converse follows by shifting smooth potentials. The normalized auxiliary density has the correct total mass, and domination gives bounded Lp uniqueness without a connected positive-density locus.

The projective block construction checks independent rank-one directions, equality of the two scalar triple products, global extension and the exact correction restoring a positive nonclosed background. Radial families match slopes and have C1,1 potentials without an interface measure.

The thin-zero family keeps the global slope barriers and flat extension. In the quadratic-zero example, the singular slope equation gives inverse-distance exponential decay; all derivatives extend by zero although the density zeros have finite order.

The analytic example prescribes its global density first, uses smooth divided differences at both zero levels, verifies determinant cancellation and patches horizontal coefficients while preserving the radial product. The exact correction restores positivity; the density has two regular connected rank-two zero hypersurfaces. Products give rank n-1 examples, with sublevel order square root and inverse-power threshold one half.

In the final analytic example the middle component is disjoint from the outer closures; it is its closure that meets both outer closures. The remark now states that precise topology and no longer overwrites the earlier block-open-set notation.

General psh inputs stay in Chapter1; the section order exposes successively different uniqueness hypotheses and then their sharpness.

findings: Declare the compact complex manifold X and dimension before the chapter motivation; retain one auxiliary Hermitian metric and smooth volume form without repeated section setup.
Make clear how contact support supplies the subsequent domination and smaller-background mass arguments, whereas relative envelope closure uses convexity and normalized compactness.

Bounded contact support passes from smooth exponential approximants through continuous, lower semicontinuous and quasi-continuous obstacles, then degenerating positive backgrounds; preserve the fixed-background expansion and weighted capacity convergence.
The unbounded contact proof uses two cutoffs before letting their levels exhaust the nonpole set; it does not assume finite total mass.

Semipositive bounded domination requires positive mass for each bounded potential; its contact argument does not require a uniform positive lower mass. The big-background proposition has its own explicit hypothesis.
Singularity volumes belong to a fixed background and ordinary singularity type. Preserve smooth-gauge and scaling identities, and the stricter quantifier in positive lower mass.

The relative class is defined by convex competitor inequalities meaningful at common poles, in an arbitrary smooth real background; nonempty finite rooftops and ordinary-envelope equality do not require semipositivity.

The smaller-background mass theorem specializes explicitly to semipositive big theta and a model reference admitting an epsilon-theta competitor; individual positivity and the uniform lower bound must remain separate.
The infinite-mass series uses a smooth head and a tail with arbitrarily small negative curvature; relative-envelope membership and trivial multiplier ideals do not imply finite mass.
